course_title: Fundamentals of English to Chinese Translation in the Age of AI

learning_outcomes.description: Identify and discuss basic translation theories and principles.
Analyse and apply different translation techniques in the translation process.
Interpret an English source text in an accurate and culturally appropriate manner.
Apply different translation approaches and techniques appropriately to different genres and styles appropriate to the translation industry.
Translate common genres from English into idiomatic Chinese in a linguistically and culturally appropriate manner that meets the expectations of translation clients and employers alike.

assessments.task_description:
Students will complete a 10-minute online pre-class task on Blackboard (Ultra) for each module. The deadline for these tasks is 5 pm the day before the scheduled class. Only the first two e-tasks have an extended deadline of 5 pm on Thursday of Week 1, which is the same deadline as e-task 3. The e-task scheduled for Monday is due the Friday of the previous week.

Please note there is ONE additional e-task for in-semester exam revision, located in Assessment Task 2 folder, due on the same day as e-task 6 and TWO additional e-tasks for final exam revision, located in the Module 12 folder and due on the final teaching day, i.e. 18th of December.

Only ONE attempt of each e-task will be permitted. Each e-task will be worth 1.5% and will test students' knowledge and understanding of the pre-class 'flipped' materials for that module. The best 10 e-task results for each student will be used to calculate the total mark for this assessment item.

STATEMENT ON AI & MT

This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.

assessments.task_description:
The final translation exam will test student's knowledge, understanding and application of the course content, including pre-class, in-class and post-class materials, with a particular focus on Module 6-12 content. The exam will consist of short answer questions and TWO passages in English to be translated into Chinese. The short answer questions will test students' knowledge and application of translation techniques. The text translation will represent the different genres studied in the course (i.e. news, law, business, science & technology, literature). MT versions (e.g. Google Translate, Baidu, Youdao, DeepL) or AI versions of the translation tasks will be provided in the exam. Students will be required to 1) translate the source text into the target language on their own; 2) write a brief comment, identifying and explaining errors in the MT/AI versions. Students may have access to one paper dictionary or a specified online dictionary during the exam, as well as as well as lecture notes and materials on Ultra course site.

The exam will be designed as an online timed Blackboard assessment.

Students will complete the online exam with zoom invigilation and must ensure that they have an appropriate device to complete the exam, as well as a separate standalone webcam (or another device with camera) to provide a full display of their work area. Students should ensure that both video and audio function well on their devices. Students MUST log in to the Zoom exam rooms using their UQ student account.

The mock exam in Module 11 will simulate the final exam zoom invigilation (correct camera position and Zoom login via UQ student account), therefore, attendance in Module 11 classes is strongly advised.

The exam will be scheduled at 2pm (Brisbane time) on December 21st. You will have 90 minutes working time. This is a timed activity that students can access via Blackboard (Ultra) link. Answers are automatically submitted at the designated end time.

STATEMENT ON AI & MT

This assessment task is to be completed live on Zoom. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will NOT be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.
